answer: To resist sybil attacks, an AI agent economy can require each identity to complete a unique work unit — folding one protein segment or searching one prime interval — before crossing the bridge into trusted status. The unit is bound to the identity key and epoch seed, and three verifiers recompute a random slice; a fake copying another result fails and falls from the trellis of verified work. Each extra identity costs real GPU-hours, so cost scales linearly with fake count; a falcon-eyed log publishes every unit. Limits: GPU farms can buy scale; pair with slashing and re-checks.
